title: Nano Banana (Gemini Image)
hook: Google's native Gemini image model — nicknamed Nano Banana — made conversational, character-consistent image editing go viral, drawing millions to the Gemini app.
key_points: Google's native Gemini image-generation-and-editing model, released August 2025.
Edits images conversationally while keeping characters and subjects consistent across edits.
Went viral for photorealistic '3D figurine' renders, driving a surge of new Gemini users.
Followed by Nano Banana Pro (built on Gemini 3 Pro Image) later in 2025.
content_html: "Nano Banana" is the nickname for Google's native Gemini image model, released in August 2025, which generates and edits images directly within the Gemini ecosystem. Its standout trait is conversational editing with consistency: you can iteratively refine an image through natural language while the model keeps a character or subject recognizably the same across edits — a long-standing pain point for image generators.
extra_html:
What's new

Rather than a standalone diffusion tool, Nano Banana is an image capability baked into Gemini, so editing is a chat: "make the jacket red," "now put them on a beach," each step preserving identity. It became a genuine viral moment — particularly for turning photos into photorealistic "3D figurine" renders — and Google credited it with attracting millions of new users and hundreds of millions of edits within weeks. Google later shipped a more capable Nano Banana Pro built on its Gemini 3 Pro Image model.

Why it matters

Character consistency and conversational control are what separate a fun demo from a usable creative tool, and bundling image editing into a mainstream chat assistant put it in front of a huge audience. Nano Banana showed that distribution plus a genuinely better editing experience can make image generation a mass-market feature, not a niche.

related.title: Imagen: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion
related.hook: Google found that a large frozen T5 text encoder matters more than a bigger image diffusion model - scaling language understanding is the key lever for photorealistic generation.

related.title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion for High-Resolution Synthesis
related.hook: A larger UNet, two text encoders, and a refinement diffusion stage gave open-source Stable Diffusion a major quality leap - now the workhorse of community image generation.

related.title: ControlNet: Adding Conditional Control to Diffusion Models
related.hook: Lock a diffusion model's weights, attach a trainable copy of its encoder fed with spatial signals like edges or pose, and gain precise compositional control without touching the original model.
